market.conclusion: Tech is in a downtrend and the broad market is moving sideways. Money is moving into defensive sectors rather than leaving the market, so this is a time to be patient rather than to panic. No new swing entries make sense until tech stabilises or Nvidia's report clears the air.
arguments: Macro: QQQ closed at 661.75, below both its 50-day and 200-day averages, and only 25% of stocks are above their 50-day average. I give this the most weight: the market is narrow and weak.
Sectors: health care (XLV) and utilities (XLU) lead, and tech (XLK) trails at -7.94 versus SPY. That is defensive rotation, and it argues against chasing tech rebounds.
Risk backdrop: VIX is 19.3 (normal) and credit spreads are steady. There is no sign of stress in lending, which is why I see a pullback rather than a crisis.
Quant: no signal type is validated, so I give quant arguments no weight either way.
market.change_mind: If QQQ closes back above its 200-day average of 682.44, or SPY closes above $750.55, I would start looking for entries. If SPY closes below $736.90, I would turn more defensive.

deep_dive.case_for: It is a grade A business with revenue up 83.38% over the past year. At $156.14 it is below its whole value range of $193.13–$411.04, and its price-to-sales is near the bottom of its own five-year history. RSI of 22.7 says the stock is oversold.
deep_dive.case_against: The chart has lower highs and lower lows and is down 28.08% in 20 sessions. Operating margin is at a five-year peak, and unpaid customer bills grew faster than sales. Insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans. This is the first report since Jensen Huang's exit.
deep_dive.decides: The 2026-11-17 report and how price reacts afterward. A close above $169.14 would be the first sign of repair. Until then, long-term buying should be gradual and small.
